items.title: Chico Hamilton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: And I went on the band. I lasted three weeks and Gladys fired me

ctx.x: Yeah, you know. Hey man, you know, I dug in, you know. And the chorus line, they all dug that man because I’d make them kick, I’d make them work, man, I’d make them shake their ass, you know. I’d play so heavy so I put on -- and they got hooked -- they loved me, you know, loved my playing. And doing that, that’s how Lionel heard me one night and he offered me the job on his band. That’s the band with Eleanor and Marshall (Royal) here again, man, I couldn’t read a note, but he wanted me on the band so he came over…
I know the name, oh, yeah.

items.title: Chico Hamilton interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 30, 2000
items.q: And Lionel used to play, he’d go around with his sticks off the bandstand, he’d play on the floor, he’d play on the walls, he’d play all over the place. So I used to imitate him.

ctx.x: As a matter of fact he’s totally responsible I guess for me getting into music because his folks gave him a clarinet when he was around that age. So he being my best friend, I had to have a clarinet. And we were so poor though, we couldn’t afford, you could get a clarinet from the school for two dollars a semester. And it took us, man it must have took me about a whole semester to get two dollars together. But anyway, getting back to that, Lionel Hampton was very popular at that time you know. And Lionel used to…
